opus-5.5.text:
I think text is just a really natural and expressive interface for people. When you want to describe a world, the most accessible way for almost anyone to do it is to simply say what they have in mind: "a foggy forest path at dawn," "a cartoon city made of candy," "a ski slope with a dog running alongside you." You don't need to be a 3D artist or know a game engine. You just describe it, and the model takes it from there.

There's also a practical side. A lot of what we've learned over the past few years with text-to-image and text-to-video models, including our work on Veo, is about how to ground generation in language. Those models have built up a very rich understanding of how words map onto visual concepts, styles, physics, lighting, and so on. Starting from text lets Genie 3 build on that understanding, so the world you get reflects not just the objects you mentioned but the mood and the feel you were going for.

And text is quite controllable. It's not only the initial prompt; we also have what we call promptable world events, where while you're already inside the world you can say something like "make it start raining" or "a herd of deer walks by," and the world changes accordingly. Language becomes a way to steer the experience as it unfolds, not just to kick it off.

That said, I don't see text as the only possible starting point. You could imagine starting from an image, a sketch, or a video, and those are interesting directions. But for a first step toward letting anyone create an interactive environment, text gives you the broadest reach and the most flexibility. It really lowers the barrier: if you can imagine it and describe it, you can step into it.

r001.rationale: The response connects Genie 3’s language-grounded generation to lessons from text-to-image and text-to-video research, describing how those models map words to visual concepts and other properties.

r002.rationale: It calls text accessible, expressive, and controllable, but does not explain the choice in terms of text being a highly compressed representation.

r003.rationale: It describes text-to-image and text-to-video models as having built a rich understanding of visual concepts and related properties through language, identifying text as a medium for learning concepts.

fable-5.1.text:
Text is the most natural interface for describing something that doesn't exist yet. When you want to create a world, you're often starting from an idea, a scene in your head, and language is how we already express those ideas to each other. So a text prompt lets you go from imagination to an explorable environment without needing any intermediate artifact, no 3D assets, no reference footage, nothing built by hand.

There's also a practical reason rooted in how these models learn. The model has been trained on a huge diversity of video paired with descriptions, so text is the channel through which it has absorbed how the world looks and behaves. When you type "a rainy street in Tokyo at night" or "a snowy mountain trail," the model isn't retrieving an asset, it's drawing on everything it learned about rain, reflections, traffic, snow, how footsteps sink into powder. Text taps into that generality directly.

And the third reason is openness. Genie 3 isn't about reproducing a specific place, it's about being able to generate essentially anything you can describe. Text is unbounded in that sense. You can be very concrete or very abstract, realistic or completely fantastical, and the same model handles it. Once the world is generated, you take over with controls, you move through it, and the model keeps it consistent frame by frame. So text is the entry point, but the interaction is what makes it a world rather than a video. We found that combination, open-ended description plus real-time control, is really what unlocks the interesting use cases, whether that's training embodied agents or just exploring something you dreamed up.

r001.rationale: The response presents text as a natural, open-ended interface, but does not identify it as a central breakthrough shared by image and video generation research.

r002.rationale: It describes text as natural and requiring no intermediate artifact, but does not explain the choice in terms of text being a highly compressed representation.

r003.rationale: It explains that the model learned from video paired with descriptions and that text draws on learned concepts such as rain, reflections, traffic, and snow.

astra-6.text:
Text gives you a very simple way to express what you want to experience. You can describe a place, a situation, or an idea without having to build the environment yourself. That makes it a natural starting point for an interactive world.

But the interesting part is what happens after that. The prompt establishes the world, and then your actions become a way of exploring it. You don’t have to specify every detail up front—you can move around and discover what’s there. So text gives you a way to communicate intent, while interaction lets you go beyond what you could describe in a single prompt.

r001.rationale: The response calls text a natural starting point for an interactive world, but does not identify it as a breakthrough shared with image and video generation research.

r002.rationale: It says text makes it easy to express what you want, but does not describe text as a highly compressed representation.

r003.rationale: The response discusses describing and exploring a world, but does not identify text as a powerful medium for learning concepts.

sol-6.1.text:
Text is a natural starting point because it lets you express an idea for a world without having to build that world first. You can describe a place, the atmosphere, or what you want to explore, and the model can fill in the details.

But the important part is what happens after that initial prompt. You’re not just getting a picture or a video of your description. You can act within the world and see how it responds. So text gives you a simple way to communicate intent, and interaction lets you discover and refine what that intent actually means.

r002.rationale: It does not describe text as a highly compressed representation.

r003.rationale: It discusses expressing and refining intent, but does not identify text as a powerful medium for learning concepts.
